text:
alex: FYI we rolled a canary for the new kernel splitter + remap path to a small fleet. Quick headline: p50 ~ -19%, p99 ~ -11%, token cost down ~21% on our mixed prod workload.

morgan: sweet. numbers and command?

alex: run used: `./rbench --suite=hotpath_mix --seq-dist=prod --warmup=3m --iter=6000`

alex: condensed results:
```
baseline     p50=64ms p95=150ms p99=215ms cost=1.00x
split+remap  p50=52ms p95=135ms p99=192ms cost=0.79x
improvement  p50=-19% p99=-11% cost=-21%
```

tara: any correctness alerts or increased OOMs?

alex: no correctness alerts. small uptick (+3%) in peak memory on a couple kernels but within buffer. no OOMs in smoke.
sam: rollback strategy?

alex: health probe watches p99 tail per-frontier. if p99 > baseline *1.05 for 5m we flip to fallback `generic-kernel` and notify #runtime-canaries. automatic rollback exists.
deploy-bot: canary deployed by alex at 1999901234 -> targets=20 hosts, traffic=4%. monitoring: #runtime-canaries
morgan: did you check model family variance (instruction-tuned vs chatty long-turns)?
alex: short-turn chat gets the largest p50 wins (~22-26%). long-turn, attention-heavy sequences get smaller latency wins but still cost reductions ~10-15% due to reduced KV thrash.
tara: Dedicated customers impacted? any UI/opt-out?
alex: runtime default enables it. we'll expose "disable-hot-split" toggle in Dedicated console for 1.0. no infra changes needed.
sam: propose rollout: 4% -> 12% (24h) -> 35% (48h) -> 100% with health gates and debug logs enabled at 12% for 48h.
alex: agreed. I'll create the rollout ticket and attach perf traces: <https://internal.redwood/bench/1999901234-summary>
morgan: awesome. can we get a one-liner for all-hands + slide?
alex: yes, will post by EOD. :tada:
deploy-bot: canary health at 1999901320: p50 delta -18%, p99 delta -10%
tara: tagging infra to watch perf counters @infra-team
alex: thanks folks. will update thread with full 48h report. Ping me in #runtime-canaries if you see anomalies.
